items.stem:

items.stem:
Meera is studying the use of LPG cylinders among 500 households in and around Pune. She has a small budget, and most respondents are daily-wage workers with little time.
(i) Which method of collecting primary data would you suggest? (ii) Give two reasons. (iii) Suggest one question for her questionnaire that is clear and not leading.
items.answer: (i) Personal interview (with a short questionnaire), possibly on a sample (ii) respondents may not fill forms themselves; clarification possible; high response (iii) e.g. "Which fuel does your household mainly use for cooking? (LPG / wood / kerosene / other)"
items.markingKey: (i) 1 mark; (ii) 2 marks; (iii) 1 mark.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Sampling error can be reduced by increasing the sample size.
Reason (R): A larger sample is closer to the population.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The weekly pocket money (₹) of five workers are 100, 175, 250, 325, 525. Aditi takes a sample of two workers with values 175 and 525. Find the sampling error of the sample mean.
items.answer: Sampling error = 350 − 275 = 75
items.markingKey: Population mean = 1375/5 = 275; sample mean = 700/2 = 350; sampling error = sample mean − population mean = 75.

items.stem: A class has 200 students. A sample of 5 students is drawn by the lottery method. What is the chance that a particular student is selected?
items.markingKey: Each student has an equal chance: 5/200 = 1/40.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: The daily wages (₹) of five workers are 200, 250, 350, 400, 625. Kavya takes a sample of two workers with values 400 and 250. Find the sampling error of the sample mean.
items.answer: Sampling error = 325 − 365 = −40
items.markingKey: Population mean = 1825/5 = 365; sample mean = 650/2 = 325; sampling error = sample mean − population mean = −40.
